name: Zostel Rishikesh (Tapovan)
summary: A backpacker hostel in Tapovan, between Lakshman Jhula and Ram Jhula, with dorms, private rooms, a rooftop cafe and a common lounge looking over the hills and the Ganga. Good for solo travellers and students starting a Garhwal trip.
body: Zostel is India's best-known hostel chain, and its Tapovan property sits on the bypass road above the cafe district, a short walk downhill to the river, yoga studios and the Lakshman Jhula area. It offers mixed and women-only dorms alongside private rooms, some with balconies, and a rooftop cafe serving Indian and global food. The common lounge has games and a work corner, and evenings often end around a bonfire.

It suits travellers who want company: rafting partners, someone to share a taxi to Neer Garh, or advice on the 5 am bus to Badrinath. It is not a quiet retreat, and the chain's policies generally exclude guests under 18, so families should look elsewhere. Book early for weekends and the March yoga festival, when Rishikesh's hostels fill.
why: Dorm beds from about ₹500 in a walkable Tapovan location
Rooftop cafe and lounge make it easy to meet other travellers
Staff help with rafting, bus and trek bookings
price_band: ₹500–1,000 a dorm bed; ₹2,000–4,000 a night for a private double (indicative)

faqs.q: Is Zostel Rishikesh good for solo women?
faqs.a: Yes. Zostel offers women-only dorms at many properties, and Tapovan is busy with solo women on yoga courses. Use lockers, keep valuables with you, and walk back along lit lanes after dark. Check room types when booking.

faqs.q: Can families or children stay at Zostel Rishikesh?
faqs.a: Zostel's policies generally do not allow guests under 18, and the atmosphere is aimed at backpackers. Families are better off at a guesthouse or hotel in Tapovan or Swarg Ashram. Confirm current rules when booking.

faqs.q: How far is Zostel Tapovan from the bus stand?
faqs.a: About 6–7 km from Rishikesh ISBT, 20–30 minutes by auto or taxi, depending on traffic. For 5 am Char Dham buses, book a taxi the night before or sleep near the ISBT the last night.

name: GMVN Tourist Rest House, Ghangaria
image_query: Ghangaria village Valley of Flowers base
summary: The state tourism corporation's rest house in Ghangaria, the base village for the Valley of Flowers and Hemkund Sahib, with simple rooms and dorm beds at government rates. Basic, but well placed and in high demand from June to September.
body: Garhwal Mandal Vikas Nigam, the Uttarakhand government's tourism corporation for Garhwal, runs rest houses along the pilgrim and trekking routes, and its Ghangaria property is one of the most useful. It sits in the village at 3,049 m, close to the forest checkpost for the Valley of Flowers and the path to Hemkund Sahib, so you can be on the trail by 7 am.

Expect a plain room with blankets, a simple dining hall and hot water that may come by the bucket. Electricity and water supply can be irregular in a village reached only on foot, and rooms get booked months ahead for July and August. It is the right choice for saver and student trips, and for anyone who values location over comfort. Book through GMVN's official channels.
why: Government rates in a village where prices rise with every step
Close to the Valley of Flowers checkpost and the Hemkund path
Dorm beds make it workable for students and solo trekkers
price_band: ₹1,500–3,500 a night for a double; dorm beds lower (indicative)

faqs.q: How do I book the GMVN rest house in Ghangaria?
faqs.a: Through GMVN's official online booking or its reservation office in Dehradun or Rishikesh. Book as soon as your dates are fixed for July and August. Avoid third-party agents who add mark-ups. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Does GMVN Ghangaria have hot water?
faqs.a: Hot water is usually available, often by the bucket at set hours rather than from a geyser on demand. Electricity can be intermittent. Bring a headlamp, a power bank and warm clothes for evenings.

faqs.q: Is food available at GMVN Ghangaria?
faqs.a: There is usually a simple dining hall serving dal, rice, roti and sabzi, and Ghangaria has many dhabas and the gurdwara langar nearby. Carry snacks for the Valley of Flowers and Hemkund days, as there is little food on those trails.

name: GMVN Hotel Devlok, Badrinath
summary: GMVN's hotel in Badrinath, one of the state corporation's two properties in the town, with plain heated rooms within walking distance of the temple. A reliable, fairly priced base for one or two nights on the yatra.
body: Badrinath fills to bursting in May and June, and many private hotels raise prices sharply. GMVN, the state tourism corporation, runs Hotel Devlok here alongside a cheaper Yatri Niwas with dorm beds. Devlok's rooms are simple but clean, with bedding suited to nights near freezing, and the walk to the temple and Tapt Kund is short.

Book early for the first month of the yatra and for September and October weekends. The restaurant serves plain vegetarian food, in keeping with the town. If Devlok is full, the Yatri Niwas suits saver travellers, and dharamshalas near the temple offer basic rooms. For more comfort, our comfort itineraries usually sleep at Joshimath or Auli and visit Badrinath with an early start.
why: Government pricing in a town where peak rates jump
Walking distance to the temple, Tapt Kund and the Mana road
Sister property Yatri Niwas offers cheaper dorm beds
price_band: ₹2,500–5,500 a night for a double in season (indicative)

faqs.q: Is GMVN Devlok close to Badrinath temple?
faqs.a: Yes, it is within walking distance of the temple and Tapt Kund. The walk involves some slope and the bridge over the Alaknanda; seniors may want to take it slowly at 3,300 m.

faqs.q: When is GMVN Devlok open?
faqs.a: It operates during the Badrinath yatra season, roughly from the temple's opening in late April or May to its closing in November. The town is snowbound and closed in winter. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Does Badrinath GMVN have dorm beds?
faqs.a: Dorm beds are offered at GMVN's Yatri Niwas in Badrinath rather than at Devlok. They suit saver travellers and students. Book through GMVN's official channels, especially for May and June.

name: Aloha on the Ganges
summary: A riverside hotel on the Badrinath road in Tapovan, near Lakshman Jhula, with rooms and apartments facing the Ganga, an outdoor pool, a spa and a restaurant. Our usual comfort pick in Rishikesh.
body: Aloha on the Ganges stands on the river side of the highway in Tapovan, run by Leisure Hotels, a group with several properties in Uttarakhand. Rooms and one- and two-bedroom apartments step down the bank towards the Ganga, and the outdoor pool and terraces look across to the forested far shore. A spa offers massages and ayurvedic treatments, and yoga sessions can be arranged.

The location works for walking to the Lakshman Jhula and Tapovan cafes and for early starts up the Badrinath road. As in all of Rishikesh, food is vegetarian and the town is alcohol-free. Ask for a river-facing room, and book early for March, October and long weekends, when Delhi visitors fill the town.
why: River-facing rooms and pool on the Ganga in Tapovan
Apartments suit families travelling together
Close to Lakshman Jhula cafes and the Badrinath road

faqs.q: Does Aloha on the Ganges have a swimming pool?
faqs.a: Yes, it has an outdoor pool on the river side. Pool hours and seasonal closures vary, so confirm when you book, especially in winter months.

faqs.q: Can I walk to Lakshman Jhula from Aloha on the Ganges?
faqs.a: Yes. The hotel is in Tapovan near Lakshman Jhula, a few minutes by car or a short walk along the road, and the Ram Jhula area is about 3 km away.

faqs.q: Is Aloha on the Ganges good for families?
faqs.a: Yes. Its apartments suit families, the pool keeps children busy, and the location is close to the riverside walks. Watch children near the river and on the hotel's terraced steps.

name: Rokeby Manor
summary: A restored 1840s stone estate on the Landour ridge near Char Dukan and St Paul's Church, now a small heritage hotel with wood-floored rooms, a cafe and quiet gardens among the deodars. The best base for walking Landour.
body: Rokeby Manor dates from the 1840s, when Landour was a young sanatorium town, and takes its name from Sir Walter Scott's poem Rokeby. In the twentieth century it served as a guest house run by Methodist missionaries before being restored as a boutique hotel. The stone walls, fireplaces, wooden floors and sloping roofs of the old house have been kept.

Its location is the point: a few minutes' walk from Char Dukan, St Paul's Church and the start of the Landour loop, away from the noise of Mussoorie's Mall. Rooms are individual in size and style, and the hotel runs a cafe and restaurant on site. Book early for October to December, when Landour's clear-day views and fireside evenings draw repeat guests.
why: In Landour itself, steps from Char Dukan and the ridge walk
Restored nineteenth-century building with fireplaces and gardens
Quiet, far from the Mall Road crowds

faqs.q: How far is Rokeby Manor from Mussoorie Mall Road?
faqs.a: About 4–5 km uphill, 15–20 minutes by car. Taxis drop you at the hotel. Most guests stay on the Landour ridge and go down to the Mall only once.

faqs.q: Is Rokeby Manor good for a winter stay?
faqs.a: Yes. Rooms are heated and many have fireplaces, and winter brings the clearest snow-peak views from Landour. Roads can ice after snowfall in January and February; follow the hotel's advice on arrival times.

faqs.q: Is Rokeby Manor suitable for children?
faqs.a: Older children who enjoy walking will like Landour. The hotel is small and quiet, with steps and slopes around the property, so it suits families with teenagers more than toddlers.

name: WelcomHeritage Kasmanda Palace
summary: A white nineteenth-century mansion above the Mall Road, built in 1836 as part of the Christ Church complex and bought in 1915 by the royal family of Kasmanda as a summer house. Now a heritage hotel with gardens and period rooms.
body: Kasmanda Palace was built in 1836 by Captain Rennie Tailour of the Bengal Engineers as part of the Christ Church complex. It later served as a sanatorium for British soldiers and, from 1896 to 1910, as a school, before the ruling family of Kasmanda, a former estate in Oudh, bought it in 1915 for their summers in the hills. It is now operated by WelcomHeritage.

The house sits in its own grounds above the Mall near Christ Church, close enough to walk into town but set apart from the crowds. Rooms keep a period feel, and the garden and terrace look down the valley. It suits travellers who want character and a central location, and it pairs well with a night or two in Landour.
why: Central location above the Mall, walkable to Christ Church and the Library end
Genuine nineteenth-century building with royal-era interiors
Garden and terrace with valley views

faqs.q: Is Kasmanda Palace on Mussoorie Mall Road?
faqs.a: It sits in its own grounds just above the Mall Road, near Christ Church, so you can walk to the Mall and the Library end. The final approach is a short climb or drive up a private road.

faqs.q: What is the history of Kasmanda Palace?
faqs.a: It was built in 1836 as part of the Christ Church complex, later used as a sanatorium and a school, and bought by the royal family of Kasmanda in 1915 as a summer residence. Today it is a WelcomHeritage hotel.

faqs.q: Is Kasmanda Palace good for a family holiday?
faqs.a: Yes. Its central location, gardens and heritage rooms suit families, and the Mall, Camel's Back Road and Company Garden are close. Ask for a room size that fits your group when booking.

name: Ananda in the Himalayas
image_query: Ananda in the Himalayas Viceregal Palace Narendra Nagar
summary: India's first destination spa, opened in 2000 on the 100-acre estate of the Tehri royal palace at Narendra Nagar, above Rishikesh. Yoga, ayurveda and Vedanta programmes with spa therapies, set among sal forest with views down to the Ganga.
body: Ananda occupies part of the estate of the Maharaja of Tehri Garhwal at Narendra Nagar, the royal capital from 1919. Its Viceregal Palace was built in 1910–11 for an expected visit by the Viceroy, which never took place; Lord Mountbatten later stayed there. Around it, guest rooms, suites and villas sit in forest on a ridge looking down towards Rishikesh and the Ganga valley.

Ananda was established in 2000 as India's first destination spa and combines yoga, meditation, ayurveda and Vedanta with international spa treatments. Guests usually follow a programme set after a consultation, from stress management to detox, though shorter stays are possible. Food is health-focused and the atmosphere is quiet. It is the signature base for our Rishikesh wellness journeys.
why: Royal Tehri estate with the 1910–11 Viceregal Palace
Full yoga and ayurveda programmes with consultations
Forest setting above Rishikesh, 30–40 minutes from the river
price_band: ₹45,000–1,00,000 a night for a double, depending on programme and room (indicative)

faqs.q: Where is Ananda in the Himalayas?
faqs.a: At Narendra Nagar, on the hill above Rishikesh, about 30–40 minutes by car from the town and about an hour from Dehradun's Jolly Grant airport. The estate belongs to the former Tehri royal family.

faqs.q: Do I need to join a programme at Ananda?
faqs.a: Many guests choose a wellness programme, which usually has a minimum stay and includes consultations, treatments and meals. Shorter stays without a full programme may be possible. Check current offers with the resort when booking.

faqs.q: Can I visit the Ganga ghats from Ananda?
faqs.a: Yes. Rishikesh's ghats, Ram Jhula and the evening aarti are 30–40 minutes away by car. The resort can arrange transfers, and we often include an evening at Triveni Ghat or Parmarth Niketan.

name: Taj Rishikesh Resort & Spa
summary: A Taj resort on 13 acres above the Ganga at Singthali, about 30 km upstream of Rishikesh, with rooms and villas facing the river and mountains, a J Wellness Circle spa, yoga and meditation. Quiet, river-focused luxury.
body: Taj Rishikesh sits on terraces above a bend of the Ganga at Singthali village, upstream of the rafting stretches and away from the town's crowds. Rooms and villas are laid out in clusters across the 13-acre site so that each looks at the river or the hills.

The J Wellness Circle spa offers massages, yoga and meditation, and the resort can arrange rafting and evening visits to the aarti in Rishikesh. It is a 30 km drive from town, about an hour on the Badrinath road, and around 1.5 hours from Jolly Grant airport. Use it as the first and last nights of a Char Dham or Valley of Flowers journey, or for a slow stay in its own right.
why: Every room and villa faces the Ganga or the hills
Upstream of Rishikesh, quiet and away from traffic
Spa, yoga and meditation on site

faqs.q: How far is Taj Rishikesh from Rishikesh town?
faqs.a: About 30 km upstream at Singthali, roughly an hour by road along the Badrinath highway. Jolly Grant airport is about 1.5 hours away. The resort arranges transfers.

faqs.q: Can I go rafting from Taj Rishikesh?
faqs.a: Yes. Rafting stretches such as Marine Drive and Shivpuri lie between the resort and Rishikesh, and the resort can arrange trips with licensed operators from mid-September to June. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is Taj Rishikesh good for a Char Dham journey?
faqs.a: Yes. It sits on the road towards Devprayag and the dhams, so it works as a comfortable first or last night, saving an hour of driving compared with staying in town.

name: JW Marriott Mussoorie Walnut Grove Resort & Spa
image_query: Mussoorie valley Kempty Falls road hills
summary: A large resort at Siya village on the Kempty Falls road, west of Mussoorie, with valley-view rooms and suites, a spa, an indoor pool, several restaurants and a bowling alley. The most complete luxury hotel in the Mussoorie hills.
body: The JW Marriott sits on a forested slope at Siya village on the Kempty Falls road, about 1 km from the falls and a short drive from Mussoorie's Library end. Rooms and suites have balconies over the Aglar valley and the hills, and the resort has a full-service spa, an indoor pool, a health club, a children's pool and several restaurants, as well as a bowling alley.

Its scale and facilities make it ideal for families and for travellers who want a resort day between sightseeing. It is also well placed for the Yamunotri road, which runs north from Kempty towards Barkot. Being outside town, it stays quieter than the Mall on busy weekends, though Mussoorie's traffic still affects the drive in and out at peak times.
why: Full resort facilities including spa and indoor pool
Valley-view balconies away from the Mall crowds
On the Kempty road, convenient for Yamunotri

faqs.q: How far is JW Marriott from Mussoorie Mall Road?
faqs.a: It is on the Kempty Falls road at Siya village, roughly 20–30 minutes by car from the Library end of the Mall, depending on traffic. The resort can arrange cars into town.

faqs.q: Does JW Marriott Mussoorie have an indoor pool?
faqs.a: Yes, the resort has an indoor pool along with a spa, health club and children's pool. Timings and access vary by season; confirm when booking.

faqs.q: Is JW Marriott Mussoorie good for kids?
faqs.a: Yes. With an indoor pool, children's pool, bowling alley and space to roam, it suits families well. Kempty Falls is about 1 km away for a short outing.
